feature_request:
Build a small library catalog system:
● A base class LibraryItem with protected members title (string) and id (int), a constructor that initializes
both, and a protected function describe() that returns a formatted string such as "ID: 3, Title: The
Hobbit".
● A derived class Book that adds author (string) and pages (int). Its constructor must chain to LibraryItem's
constructor, and it should have a display() function that calls describe() (inherited and protected, so it is
directly usable inside Book) and then prints the author and page count.
● A derived class Magazine that adds issueNumber (int) and month (string). Its constructor must also chain
to LibraryItem's constructor, and it should have its own display() function.
C++ Lab (DSAI/ECE)
● In main(), create one Book object and one Magazine object directly, and call display() on each to print
the full details.
Submit the code and the program's output
acceptance_criteria: LibraryItem initializes protected title and id members correctly.
Book constructor chains to LibraryItem and stores author, pages.
Book display prints inherited description plus author and pages.
Magazine constructor chains to base and stores issue, month.
Main creates objects and prints their full display details.

NEW FILE: library_catalog.cpp

This C++ lab assignment requires implementing a class hierarchy and a main function within C++. The existing repository consists entirely of Python files (bank_account.py, banking.py, hello.py, etc.). 

1. Create a new file `library_catalog.cpp`.
2. Define the base class `LibraryItem` with protected members `title` (string) and `id` (int). Implement a constructor for initialization and a protected virtual function `describe()` returning the formatted string "ID: 3, Title: The Hobbit".
3. Define the derived class `Book` inheriting from `LibraryItem`. Add private/protected members `author` (string) and `pages` (int). The constructor must chain to `LibraryItem`. Implement a `display()` method that calls `describe()` and prints the author and page count.
4. Define the derived class `Magazine` inheriting from `LibraryItem`. Add members `issueNumber` (int) and `month` (string). The constructor must chain to `LibraryItem`. Implement a `display()` method that prints the issue number and month (and presumably calls `describe()` for full details based on the pattern in Book).
5. Implement `main()` to instantiate one `Book` and one `Magazine` and call `display()` on each to verify output.
